Sam (People Ops): Heads up — Fidelity just emailed saying theyre sunsetting the ZeroFee Retirement platform for small plans. Vendor claims termination effective next month. Anyone seen this yet?
Nina (Payroll): Yikes. I saw the vendor notice in my inbox an hour ago. It mentioned participant transfers and trustee instructions but no clear dates for payroll stop.
Jasper (Benefits Admin): I opened the notice. It says plan-level termination date 2023-10-15 and gives a 30-day window for participant transfers. No automated payroll webhook mentioned.
Sam (People Ops): Ok — two immediate questions: 1) what happens to ongoing pre-tax deferrals and catch-up contributions? 2) loans/loan repayments in-flight?
Nina (Payroll): 1) We stop sending deferrals to that plan on the payroll date after the plan termination is processed. So if termination processed 10/15, contributions in the next pay run would need a remapping or stop. We can hold a small off-cycle if needed.
Jasper (Benefits Admin): 2) Loans: vendor says outstanding loans become owed to the participants account automatically (i.e., outstanding balance due as taxable distribution) unless transferred to successor trustee. They provided a transfer packet and a trustee-to-trustee transfer form.
Sam (People Ops): Does that mean affected folks might get a taxable event if we don't move balances? That would suck.
Alex (Legal): Potentially yes. We need to avoid inadvertent taxable distributions. Check whether the successor trustee accepts in-plan loan transfers or requires rollovers. We should also confirm participant notices and opt-out windows for deferral changes.
BenefitsBot: Doc: Transition checklist -> https://intranet.redwood/benefits/retirement-vendor-termination-checklist (internal)
Sam (People Ops): Action items I propose: A) Pause new deferral changes for affected plan until we confirm routing B) Run list of active participants with loans and after-tax/roth balances C) Coordinate off-cycle remap or transfer with payroll vendor D) Draft participant notice by EOD. Thoughts?
Nina (Payroll): I can export the participant deferral feed CSV tonight: `employee_id,name,ssn,last_deferral_amount,loan_balance` then run a mock payroll to see impact. If we need off-cycle we'll need approvals — payroll cutoffs are 3 business days before pay date.
Jasper (Benefits Admin): I'll request the successor trustees intake requirements and whether they support direct trustee-to-trustee rollovers for loans. If they do, we can avoid distributions. Also request the PDF transfer form and a batch API spec.
Alex (Legal): I'll review the termination notice and vendor agreements for mandatory notification windows and any indemnity language. If vendor missed a contractual notice period, we might have leverage to delay processing.
Sam (People Ops): Cool. For participant communication: short urgent note first: "Fidelity is ending support for ZeroFee Retirement for Redwood employees on 10/15. We are working to transfer accounts; please DO NOT change contribution elections until we confirm." Then follow-up with detailed FAQs. Jasper/Nina can you have drafts by 3pm?
Jasper (Benefits Admin): Yes, I have a plain-language FAQ template. Will add loan/rollover Qs and the transfer form link.
Nina (Payroll): Ill run the export and post a few sample rows (redacted) so ops can see edge cases.
BenefitsBot: Reminder set: @Sam @Nina @Jasper check-in 2pm today.
Sam (People Ops): If successor trustee expects signed participant forms, we need to decide whether Redwood will help collect signatures or require employees to sign and submit. Collecting signatures centrally is faster but operationally heavier. Thoughts?
Alex (Legal): From a privacy/compliance perspective, we can host a signed form upload endpoint in the console for employees; collection is ok if we document consent and retention. I'll draft a short consent blurb.
Jasper (Benefits Admin): Prefer central collection if we can automate verification — reduces risk of lost forms and speeds batch transfers. I'll confirm with the trustee whether electronic signatures are accepted.
Sam (People Ops): Great. Next steps: Jasper confirm trustee intake + e-sign tolerance by 2pm; Nina post CSV snapshot by 1:30pm; Alex legal blurb by 3pm; I'll assemble the urgent all-employee note after 3pm for 4pm send. Thanks team. :pray:
Nina (Payroll): Upload done: sample rows below (redacted):
```
employee_id,name,last_deferral_amount,loan_balance
10023,REDACTED,500,12000
10087,REDACTED,0,0
10199,REDACTED,250,4500
```
Jasper (Benefits Admin): Trustee confirmed acceptance of electronic batch transfers and e-signatures. They want a batch CSV with `ssn,last4,dob,account_type,amount_to_transfer` plus signed participant consent PDF per participant.
Sam (People Ops): Ok that's workable. Anyone expect major friction with catch-up contributions (50+ participants)?
Nina (Payroll): We'll flag catch-up contributors and include them in the transfer mapping. For any pay periods where contributions clear after termination, we'll either redirect to successor plan or hold until employee confirms next election.
Alex (Legal): Also note cross-border participants — some need country-specific tax treatment. Jasper add a section in the FAQ for international employees.
Sam (People Ops): Thanks. I'll send a brief status update to leadership and post the urgent note company-wide once we have the consent language. I'll keep this thread as the master log.
Jasper (Benefits Admin): Uploaded transfer packet and draft FAQ to the shared drive: `Shared/Benefits/ZeroFee-Transition/`
BenefitsBot: thread archived in 48 hours unless reopened."
